Q: VS Code: Persistent R or Python sessions over SSH A:

The only way I've been able to figure out how to do this is to first open a tmux terminal and then start R from within the tmux terminal.

Install tmux on the server, then you can open a bash terminal from within vscode and type tmux new -s SESSION_NAME Then from within that tmux session type R Now when you want to close your laptop but keep whatever running on the server, close the tmux window with the keystroke Ctl+b then d. Now when you want to access the session again you open a bash terminal and type tmux a -t SESSION_NAME and then you're right back where you left off

Q: How to match any amount of unicode characters ( letters, numbers, surrogate Pairs) in regex: A:

Are you trying to match non-ascii characters? No, because "abc123".

Are you trying to match non-whitespace characters? Your implementation of regex may have a predefined escape or character class for that (e.g. Python with \S).

But a lot of the fine detail will depend on which implementation of regex in which language you are using (just saying regex does not identify a well-defined thing), settings and data types used. So, do you have some code?

Q: How to set StreamReadConstraints in Jackson 3 (Spring Boot 4) A:

Possible solutions

Introduction

Please, see the related GitHub issues:

  • Provide configuration properties and customizers for configuring Jackson's factories · Issue #34709 · spring-projects/spring-boot.
  • JsonMapper.Builder cannot be auto-configured with a custom JsonFactory · Issue #48594 · spring-projects/spring-boot.

They are referred to in the following sections.

Straightforward (permanent?) solution (GitHub issue #34709)

It looks like the scope of the GitHub issue #34709 includes providing the customizer support for configuring the JsonFactory Jackson factory, according to the comments:

  • The comment:

    wilkinsona on Jan 20, 2026 Member

    Superseded by #34709.

    We'll address this in Spring Boot 4.1 with full property and customiser-based support for configuring Jackson's JsonFactory (and CBORFactory and XMLFactory). In the meantime, defining a custom mapper bean as shown above is the recommended approach.

  • The comment:

    wilkinsona on Jan 20, 2026 Member

    We discussed this issue and #48594 yesterday. We're going to broaden the scope of this issue to provide configuration property and customizer support for configuring Jackson's factories (CBORFactory, JsonFactory, and XMLFactory).

Therefore, the solution is:

  1. To wait for a next Spring Boot release with the resolved GitHub issue #34709.
  2. To use the mentioned customizer support provided in the release.

Temporary (current) solution

Reference #1 (GitHub issue #34709)

It looks like effectively the same question was asked here: the comment:

csensenbw on Dec 3, 2025 · edited by csensenbw

This works pretty good for Spring Boot 3. But I didn't found a way to migrate this code to Spring Boot 4. The migration guide recomends to replace "Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer" with "JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer". But "JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer" doesn't offer any postConfigurer methods.

Any suggestions?

original code:
@Bean
    fun customStreamReadConstraints(): Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer =
        Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer { builder ->
            builder.postConfigurer { objectMapper ->
                objectMapper.factory.setStreamReadConstraints(
                    StreamReadConstraints.builder().maxStringLength(maxStringLengthMbytes * 1024 * 1024).build(),
                )
            }
        }

It looks like here is the answer to the question, which contains the solution: the comment:

wilkinsona on Dec 8, 2025 Member

Thanks, both.

@csensenbw, in Spring Boot 4.0, that translates to having to define your own JsonMapper.Builder with a custom JsonFactory. You can keep all the existing property-based customisation by applying any JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer beans to that builder.

Something like this:

@Bean
@Scope(ConfigurableBeanFactory.SCOPE_PROTOTYPE)
JsonMapper.Builder jsonMapperBuilder(List<JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer> customizers) {
  JsonFactory jsonFactory = JsonFactory.builder()
      .streamReadConstraints(StreamReadConstraints.builder().maxNameLength(75000).build())
      .build();
  JsonMapper.Builder builder = JsonMapper.builder(jsonFactory);
  customizers.forEach((customizer) -> customizer.customize(builder));
  return builder;
}

Reference #2 (GitHub issue #48594)

Here effectively the same solution (as the one described in the «Reference #1» section) is provided and it is noted that, currently, this is the recommended approach:

  • The comment:

    wilkinsona on Jan 2, 2026 Member

    I'm not sure that this should have been fixed as a bug, particularly as it may limit our options for #34709 where Boot could, perhaps, starting auto-configuring a JsonFactory itself.

    As things stand, you can, with a little bit of friction, already use a custom JsonFactory:

    @Bean
@Scope(ConfigurableBeanFactory.SCOPE_PROTOTYPE)
JsonMapper.Builder jsonMapperBuilder(List<JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer> customizers) {
  JsonFactory jsonFactory = … // create custom factory
  JsonMapper.Builder builder = JsonMapper.builder(jsonFactory);
  customizers.forEach((customizer) -> customizer.customize(builder));
  return builder;
}

    I wonder if we should consider this to be good enough for 4.0.x. At the least, I think we should decide what to do with #34709 before changing 4.0.x just to be sure that we haven't limited our options for the future.

Q: Window is smaller than requested in CreateWindowExW() A:

Older Windows versions had thicker frames. When making them thinner, the client area was kept the same (for one choice of compatibility). So, the size includes the frame that the window once had.

Q: Mapping UML Association class to Java Model code A:

One easy way to implement an association class is to use a Collection<CourseEnrollment> e.g. an ArrayList<CourseEnrollment>, in both Course and Student, and make sure that CourseEnrollment has a property back to the respective Course and Student.

The navigation would then be indirect: Student -> List of enrolments -> corresponding courses, or Course -> List of enrolments -> corresponding students. The challenge in your code will be to maintain consistency, e.g. if your remove a student from a course, you'll need not only to delete the enrollment from the course's collection, but also from the student's collection.

Another alternative is to use an independent repository of CourseEnrollments, that keeps a list of all the enrolments and provides efficient access for a student and a course, through two HashMap. The advantage is that there's only one place to manage the enrollment, and students or courses can get the relevant and up-to-date links from there. Again, navigation is indirect, this time by querying the repository. The challenge here is to manage decoupling, since every Student or Course would need to know about the repository.

You may have noticed, that in both cases, the trick is to implement the association class as a class, and to decompose the direct association between Student and Course into an indirect association via the association class.

P.S: In the UML semantics, the association class is at the same time a class and an association. But it can have only one name. Chose either chooses or CourseEnrollment, but you should not use different names.
